**Quit stays quit (Linux)**
- Quitting the wallpaper from the menu now stops it for good, as the tray's Quit does. Before, the menu's Quit only closed the program, and the service that keeps the wallpaper going (it restarts it after the monitor sleeps, say) started it again a few seconds later.
- Both now stop the service by name, even when the app can't tell it's running under it, and note the quit, so a wallpaper started again in the next minute closes itself instead of coming back. It starts as usual at the next login, or when set up again from the menu.

**Easing off on a computer that struggles**
- The wallpaper now watches what it costs: its own processor time, and on Linux the kitty terminal drawing it, which without a working graphics driver can be most of the cost. Over 40% of a core, it lowers its frame rate a step at a time (30, 24, 20, 15, 12, 10). Once it's light again for half a minute, it comes back up, never past the frame rate chosen.
- Menu → Desktop shows it beside the frame rate ("easing off: 15 now"), with a switch to turn it off (*Ease off the frame rate when the computer struggles*, on by default).
- The wallpaper's log says when it eases off and what the cost was, split between the village and kitty, for finding where an older computer's time goes.
